passages.text: Amphitryon: What mortal has not heard of the one who shared a wife with Zeus, Amphitryon of Argos, whom once Alcaeus, son of Perseus, begot, Amphitryon the father of Heracles? Who lived here in Thebes , where from the sowing
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: of the dragon’s teeth grew up a crop of earth-born giants; and of these Ares saved a scanty band, and their children’s children people the city of Cadmus. Hence sprung Creon, son of Menoeceus, king of this land;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and Creon became the father of this lady Megara, whom once all Cadmus’ race escorted with the glad music of lutes at her wedding, when the famous Heracles led her to my halls. Now he, my son, left Thebes where I was settled, left his wife Megara and her kin,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: eager to make his home in Argolis , in that walled town which the Cyclopes built, from which I am exiled for the slaying of Electryon; so he, wishing to lighten my affliction and to find a home in his own land, offered Eurystheus a mighty price for my recall:
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: to free the world of savage monsters, whether it was that Hera goaded him to submit to this, or that fate was leagued against him. Other toils he has accomplished, and last of all has he passed through the mouth of Taenarus into the halls of Hades to drag to the light
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: that hound with three bodies, and from there he has never returned. Now there is an ancient legend among the race of Cadmus that a certain Lycus in days gone by was husband to Dirce, and he was king of this city with its seven towers, before Amphion and Zethus, sons of Zeus,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: lords of the milk-white steeds, became rulers in the land. His son, called by the same name as his father, although no Theban but a stranger from Euboea , slew Creon, and after that seized the government, having fallen on this city when weakened by dissension.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: So this family connection with Creon is likely to prove to us a serious evil; for now that my son is in the bowels of the earth, this new monarch Lycus is bent on extirpating the children of Heracles,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: to quench one bloody feud with another, likewise his wife and me, if useless age like mine is to rank among men, that the boys may never grow up to exact a blood-penalty of their uncle’s family. So I, left here by my son, while he is gone into the pitchy darkness of the earth,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: to tend and guard his children in his house, am taking my place with their mother, that the race of Heracles may not perish, here at the altar of Zeus the Savior, which my own gallant child set up
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: to commemorate his glorious victory over the Minyae. And here we are careful to keep our station, though in need of everything, of food, drink and clothes, huddled together on the hard bare ground; for we are barred out from our house and sit here for want of any other safety.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: As for friends, some I see are unreliable; while others, who are staunch, have no power to help us further. This is what misfortune means to man; may it never fall to the lot of any who bears the least goodwill to me, to apply this never-failing test of friendship!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Megara: Old warrior, who once razed the citadel of the Taphians leading on the troops of Thebes to glory, how uncertain are the gods’ dealings with man! I, for instance, as far as concerned my father, was never an outcast of fortune, for he was once accounted a man of might by reason of his wealth,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: possessed as he was of royal power, for which long spears are launched at the lives of the fortunate through love of it; children too he had; and he gave me to your son, matching me in glorious marriage with Heracles. And now all that is dead and gone from us;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and I and you, old friend, are doomed to die, and these children of Heracles, whom I am guarding beneath my wing as a bird keeps her tender chicks under her. And they one after another keep asking me: Mother, tell us, where is our father gone from the land?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: what is he doing? when will he return? Thus they inquire for their father, in childish perplexity; while I put them off with excuses, inventing stories; but still I wonder if it is he whenever a door creaks on its hinges, and up they all start, thinking to embrace their father’s knees.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: What hope or way of salvation are you now devising, old friend? for I look to you. We can never steal beyond the boundaries of the land unseen, for there is too strict a watch set on us at every outlet, nor have we any longer hopes of safety
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: in our friends. Whatever your scheme is, declare it, lest our death be made ready.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: It is by no means easy, my daughter, to give one’s earnest advice on such matters off hand, without weary thought; but let us prolong the time, since we are powerless to escape.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Megara: Do you need a further taste of grief, or do you cling so fast to life?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: Yes, I love this life, and cling to its hopes.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Megara: So do I; but you should not expect the unexpected, old friend.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: In these delays the only cure for our evils is left.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Megara: It is the biting pain of that interval I feel so.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: Daughter, there may yet be a happy escape from present troubles for me and you; my son, your husband, may yet arrive. So calm yourself, and wipe those tears from your children’s eyes, and soothe them with soft words,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: inventing a tale to delude then, piteous though such fraud be. Yes, for even men’s misfortunes often flag, and the stormy wind does not always blow so strong, nor are the prosperous ever so; for all things change, making way for each other.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: The bravest man is he who relies ever on his hopes, but despair is the mark of a coward.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: To the sheltering roof, to the old man’s couch, leaning on my staff have I set forth,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: chanting a plaintive dirge like some bird grown grey, I that am only a voice and a fancy bred of the visions of sleep by night, palsied with age, yet meaning kindly. All hail! you orphaned children!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: all hail, old friend! you too, unhappy mother, wailing for your husband in the halls of Hades!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Do not faint too soon upon your way,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: or let your limbs grow weary, as a colt beneath the yoke grows weary as he mounts some stony hill, dragging the weight of a wheeled chariot. Take hold of hand or robe, who ever feels his footsteps falter.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Old friend, escort another like yourself, who once amid his toiling peers in the days of our youth would take his place beside you, no blot upon his country’s glorious record.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: See, how like their father’s sternly flash these children’s eyes! Misfortune has not failed his children, nor yet has his comeliness been denied them.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: O Hellas ! if you lose these, of what allies will you rob yourself!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: But I see Lycus, the ruler of this land, drawing near the house.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Lycus: One question, if I may, to this father of Heracles and his wife; and certainly as your lord and master I have a right to put what questions I choose. How long do you seek to prolong your lives? What hope, what aid do you see to save you from death?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Do you trust that these children’s father, who lies dead in the halls of Hades, will return? How unworthily you show your sorrow at having to die, you to Amphitryon after your idle boasts, scattered broadcast through Hellas , that Zeus was partner in your marriage-bed and was your partner in children;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and you, to Megara after calling yourself the wife of so peerless a lord.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: After all, what was the fine exploit your husband achieved, if he did kill a water-snake in a marsh or that monster of Nemea ? which he caught in a snare, for all he says he strangled it to death in his arms.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Are these your weapons for the hard struggle? Is it for this then that Heracles’ children should be spared? A man who has won a reputation for valor in his contests with beasts, in all else a weakling;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: who never buckled shield to arm nor faced the spear, but with a bow, that coward’s weapon, was ever ready to run away. Archery is no test of manly bravery; no! he is a man who keeps his post in the ranks and steadily faces the swift wound the spear may plough.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: My policy, again, old man, shows no reckless cruelty, but caution; for I am well aware I slew Creon, the father of this woman, and am in possession of his throne. So I have no wish that these children should grow up and be left to take vengeance on me in requital for what I have done.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: Let Zeus defend his his own share in his son; but as for me, Heracles, it is my concern on your behalf to prove by what I say this tyrant’s ignorance; for I cannot allow you to be ill spoken of. First then for that which should never have been said—for to speak
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: of you, Heracles, as a coward is, I think, outside the pale of speech—of that must I clear you with heaven to witness. I appeal then to the thunder of Zeus, and the chariot in which he rode, when he pierced the Giants, earth’s brood, to the heart with his winged shafts,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and with gods uplifted the glorious triumph song; or go to Pholoe and ask the insolent tribe of four-legged Centaurs, you craven king, ask them who they would judge the bravest of men; will they not say my son, who according to you is but a pretender?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Were you to ask Euboean Dirphys, your native place, it would not sing your praise, for you have never done a single gallant deed to which your country can witness. Next you disparage that clever invention, an archer’s weapon;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: come, listen to me and learn wisdom. A man who fights in line is a slave to his weapons, and if his fellow-comrades want for courage he is slain himself through the cowardice of his neighbors, or, if he breaks his spear, he cannot defend his body from death, having only one means of defence;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: whereas all who are armed with the trusty bow, though they have but one weapon, yet is it the best; for a man, after discharging countless arrows, still has others with which to defend himself from death, and standing at a distance keeps off the enemy, wounding them for all their watchfulness with invisible shafts,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and never exposing himself to the foe, but keeping under cover; and this is by far the wisest course in battle, to harm the enemy and keep safe oneself, independent of chance. These arguments completely contradict yours
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: with regard to the matter at issue. Next, why are you desirous of slaying these children? What have they done to you? One piece of wisdom I credit you with, your coward terror of a brave man’s descendants. Still it is hard on us,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: if for your cowardice we must die; a fate that ought to have overtaken you at our braver hands, if Zeus had been fairly disposed towards us. But, if you are so anxious to make yourself supreme in the land, let us go into exile;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: abstain from all violence, else you will suffer by it whenever the god causes fortune’s breeze to veer round.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Ah! you land of Cadmus—for to you too will I turn, distributing my words of reproach—is this your defense of Heracles and his children?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: the man who faced alone all the Minyans in battle and allowed Thebes to see the light with free eyes. I cannot praise Hellas , nor will I ever keep silence, finding her so craven as regards my son; she should have come with fire and sword and warrior’s arms
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: to help these tender chicks, to requite him for all his labors in purging land and sea. Such help, my children, neither Hellas nor the city of Thebes affords you; to me a feeble friend you look, and I am empty sound and nothing more.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: For the vigor which once I had, has gone from me; my limbs are palsied with age, and my strength is decayed. If I were young and still powerful in body, I would have seized my spear and dabbled those flaxen locks of his with blood, so that the coward would now
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: be flying from my spear beyond the bounds of Atlas.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus Leader: Have not the brave among mankind a fair occasion for speech, although slow to begin?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Lycus: Say what you will of me in your exalted phrase, but I by deeds will make you rue those words.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Calling to his servants Go, some to Helicon, others to the glens of Parnassus , and bid woodmen to cut me logs of oak, and when they are brought to the town, pile up a stack of wood all round the altar on either side, and set fire to it and burn them
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: all alive, that they may learn that the dead no longer rules this land, but that for the present I am king. Angrily to the Chorus As for you, old men, since you thwart my views, not for the children of Heracles alone shall you lament, but likewise for your own
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: misfortunes, and you shall never forget you are slaves and I your prince.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: —You sons of Earth, whom Ares once sowed, when from the dragon’s ravening jaw he had torn the teeth, up with your staves, on which you lean your hands,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and dash out this villain’s brains! a fellow who, without even being a Theban, but a foreigner, lords it shamefully over the younger men; but my master shall you never be to your joy.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: —Nor shall you reap the harvest of all my toil;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Go back to where you came from, in your insolence. For never while I live, shall you slay these sons of Heracles; not so deep beneath the earth has their father disappeared from his children’s ken.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: —You are in possession of this land which you have ruined,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: while he, its benefactor, has missed his just reward.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: —And yet do I take too much upon myself because I help those I love after their death, when most they need a friend?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: —Ah! right hand, how you desire to wield the spear, but your weakness is a death-blow to your desire.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: For then I would have stopped you calling me slave, and I would have governed Thebes with credit. In which you now rejoice; for a city sick with dissension and evil counsels does not think aright; otherwise it would never have accepted you as its master.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Megara: Old men, I thank you; it is right that friends should feel virtuous indignation on behalf of those they love; but do not on our account vent your anger on the tyrant to your own undoing. Hear my advice, Amphitryon, if there appears to you to be anything in what I say.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: I love my children; strange if I did not love those whom I bore, whom I labored for! Death I count a dreadful fate; but the man who strives against necessity I esteem a fool. Since we must die, let us do so
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: without being burnt alive, a source of mockery to our enemies, which to my mind is an evil worse than death; for much good do we owe our family. You have always had a warrior’s fair fame, so it is not to be endured that you should die a coward’s death;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and my husband’s reputation needs no one to witness that he would never consent to save these children’s lives by letting them incur the stain of cowardice; for the noble are afflicted by disgrace on account of their children, nor must I shrink from following my lord’s example.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: As to your hopes consider how I weigh them. Do you think your son will return from beneath the earth? And who ever has come back from the dead out of the halls of Hades? But would you soften this man by entreaty? Oh no! better to fly from one’s enemy when he is so brutish,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: but yield to men of breeding and culture; for you would more easily conclude a friendly truce by accepting regard. True, a thought has already occurred to me that we might by entreaty obtain a sentence of exile for the children; yet this too is misery, to compass their deliverance with dire penury as the result;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: for it is a saying that hosts look sweetly on banished friends for a day and no more. Endure to die with us, for that awaits you after all. By your brave soul I challenge you, old friend; for whoever struggles hard to escape destiny sent by the gods
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: shows zeal no doubt, but it is zeal with a taint of folly; for what must be, no one will ever avail to alter.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus Leader: If a man had insulted you, while yet my arms were strong, there would have been an easy way to stop him; but now am I am nothing ; and so you henceforth, Amphitryon,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: must scheme how to avert misfortune.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: It is not cowardice or any longing for life that hinders my dying, but my wish to save my son’s children, though no doubt I am longing for the impossible. See! here is my neck ready for the sword
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: to pierce, to hack, to hurl from the rock; only one favor I crave for both of us, king; slay me and this hapless mother before you slay the children, that we may not see the hideous sight, as they gasp out their lives, calling on their mother
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and their father’s father; for the rest work your will if so you are inclined; for we have no defense against death.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Megara: I too implore you add a second favor, that by your single act you may put us both under a double obligation; allow me to deck my children in the robes of death,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: first opening the palace gates, for now we are shut out, so that this at least they may obtain from their father’s halls.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Lycus: I grant it, and bid my servants undo the bolts. Go in and deck yourselves; robes do not grudge. But as soon as you have clothed yourselves,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: I will return to you to consign you to the nether world. Exit Lycus.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Megara: Children, follow the footsteps of your hapless mother to your father’s house, where others possess his substance, though his name is still ours. Exit Megara with her children.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: O Zeus, in vain, it seems, did I get you to share my bride with me;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: in vain used we to call you partner in my son. After all you are less our friend than you pretended. Great god as you are, I, a mortal, surpass you in true worth. For I did not betray the children of Heracles; but you by stealth found your way to my bed,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: taking another’s wife without leave given, while to save your own friends you have no skill. Either you are a god of little sense, or else naturally unjust. Exit Amphitryon.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: Phoebus is singing a dirge, after his happier strains,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: for Linus dead in his beauty, striking his lyre with key of gold; but I wish to sing a song of praise, a crown to all his toil, on the one who has gone to the gloom beneath the nether world,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: whether I am to call him son of Zeus or of Amphitryon. For the virtue of noble toils is a glory to the dead.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: First he cleared the grove of Zeus
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: of a lion, and put its skin upon his back, hiding his yellow auburn hair in its fearful gaping jaws.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: And then one day with murderous bow he wounded
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: the race of wild Centaurs, that range the hills, slaying them with winged shafts. Peneus, the river of fair eddies, knows him well, and those far fields unharvested,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and the steadings on Pelion and neighboring caves of Homole, from where the Centaurs rode forth to conquer Thessaly , arming themselves with pines.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: And he slew that dappled deer with horns of gold, that preyed upon the country-folk, glorifying Artemis, huntress queen of Oenoe.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Next he mounted on a chariot and tamed with the bit the horses of Diomedes, that greedily champed their bloody food at gory mangers with unbridled jaws, devouring with hideous joy the flesh of men;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: then crossing the heights of Hebrus that flow with silver, he still toiled on for the tyrant of Mycenae .
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: And at the strand of the Pelian gulf
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: by the streams of Anaurus, he slew with his arrows Cycnus, murderer of his guests, the savage wretch who dwelt in Amphanae.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: And he came to those minstrel maids,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: to their orchard in the west, to pluck from the leafy apple-tree its golden fruit, when he had slain the tawny dragon, whose terrible coils were twined all round to guard it;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and he made his way into ocean’s lairs, bringing calm to men that use the oar.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: And he stretched out his hands to uphold the firmament,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: seeking the home of Atlas, and on his manly shoulders took the starry mansions of the gods.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Then he went through the waves of heaving Euxine against the mounted host of Amazons dwelling round Maeotis,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: the lake that is fed by many a stream, having gathered to his standard all his friends from Hellas , to fetch the gold-embroidered raiment of the warrior queen,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: a deadly quest for a girdle. Hellas won those glorious spoils of the barbarian maid, and they are safe in Mycenae .
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: He burned to ashes Lerna ’s murderous hound,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: the many-headed water-snake, and smeared its venom on his darts, with which he slew the shepherd of Erytheia, a monster with three bodies.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: And many another glorious achievement he brought to a happy issue; to Hades’ house of tears has he now sailed, the goal of his labors, where he is ending his career of toil, nor does he come back again.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Now your house is left without a friend, and Charon’s boat awaits your children to bear them on that journey out of life, without return, contrary to the gods’ law and man’s justice; and it is to your prowess
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: that your house is looking although you are not here.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Had I been strong and lusty, able to brandish the spear in battle’s onset, and my Theban companions too, I would have stood by your children
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: to champion them; but now my happy youth is gone and I am left.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus Leader: But look! I see the children of Heracles who was once so great, wearing the clothes of the dead,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and his loving wife dragging her babes along at her side, and Heracles’ aged father. Ah! woe is me! no longer can I stem the flood of tears
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: that spring to my old eyes.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Megara: Come now, who is to sacrifice or butcher these poor children? or rob me of my wretched life? These victims are ready to be led to Hades’ halls. O my children! an ill-matched company are we hurried off to die,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: old men and young ones and mothers, all together. Alas! for my sad fate and my children’s, whom these eyes now for the last time behold. So I gave you birth and reared you only for our foes to mock, to jeer at, and slay.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Ah me! how bitterly my hopes have disappointed me in the expectation I once formed from the words of your father. Addressing each of her three sons in turn. To you your dead father was for giving Argos ; and you were to dwell in the halls of Eurystheus, lording it over the fair fruitful land of Argolis ;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and over your head would he throw that lion’s skin with which he himself was armed. And you were to be king of Thebes , famed for its chariots, receiving as your heritage my broad lands, for so you coaxed your dear father;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and to your hand he used to resign the carved club, his sure defence, pretending to give it to you. And to you he promised to give Oechalia , which once his archery had wasted. Thus with three principalities
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: would your father exalt you, his three sons, proud of your manliness; while I was choosing the best brides for you, scheming to link you by marriage to Athens , Thebes , and Sparta , that you might live a happy life with a fast sheet-anchor to hold by.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: And now that is all vanished; fortune’s breeze has veered and given to you for brides the maidens of death in their stead, and my tears will be the marriage bath; woe is me for my foolish thoughts! and your grandfather here is celebrating your marriage-feast, the cares of a father, accepting Hades as the father of your brides.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Ah me! which of you shall I first press to my bosom, which last? on which bestow my kiss, or clasp close to me? Oh! would that like the bee with russet wing, I could collect from every source my sighs in one, and, blending them together, shed them in one copious flood!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: O my dearest Heracles, to you I call, if perhaps mortal voice can make itself heard in Hades’ halls; your father and children are dying, and I am doomed, I who once because of you was counted blessed as men count bliss. Come to our rescue; appear, I pray, if only as a phantom,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: since your arrival, even as a dream, would be enough, for they are cowards who are slaying your children.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: Lady, prepare the funeral rites; but I, O Zeus, stretching out my hand to heaven, call on you to help these children,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: if such is your intention; for soon any aid of yours will be unavailing; and yet you have been often invoked; my toil is in vain; death seems inevitable. You aged friends, the joys of life are few; so take heed that you pass through it as gladly as you may,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: without a thought of sorrow from morning until night; for time takes little heed of preserving our hopes; and, when he has busied himself on his own business, away he flies. Look at me, a man who had made a mark among his fellows by deeds of note; yet fortune in a single day
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: has robbed me of it as of a feather that floats away toward the sky. I know not any whose plenteous wealth and high reputation is fixed and sure; fare you well, for now you have seen the last of your old friend, my comrades.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Megara: Ah! Old friend, is it my own, my dearest I see? or what am I to say?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: I do not know, my daughter; I too am struck dumb.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Megara: Is this he who they told us was beneath the earth?It is, unless some day-dream mocks our sight. What am I saying? What visions do these anxious eyes behold? Old man, this is no one other than your own son.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Come here, my children, cling to your father’s robe, hurry, never loose your hold, for here is one to help you, not at all behind our savior Zeus.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: All hail! my house and gates of my home, how glad I am to emerge to the light and see you.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Ah! what is this? I see my children before the house in the robes of death, with chaplets on their heads and my wife amid a throng of men, and my father weeping—what misfortune? Let me draw near to them and inquire;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: lady, what strange stroke of fate has fallen on the house?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Megara: Dearest of all mankind to me!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: O ray of light appearing to your father!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Megara: Are you safe and is your coming just in time to help your dear ones?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: What do you mean? What is this confusion I find on my arrival, father?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Megara: We are being ruined; forgive me, old friend,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: if I have anticipated that to which you had a right to tell him; for women’s nature is perhaps more prone to grief than men’s and they are my children that were being led to death, which was my own lot too.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Apollo! what a prelude to your story!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Megara: My brothers are dead, and my old father.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: How so? what did he do? whose spear did he meet?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Megara: Lycus, our new monarch, slew him.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Did he meet him in fair fight, or was the land sick and weak?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Megara: Yes, from faction; now he is master of the city of Cadmus with its seven gates.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Why has panic fallen on you and my aged father?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Megara: He meant to kill your father, me, and my children.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: What are you saying? What did he have to fear from my orphan babes?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Megara: He was afraid they might some day avenge Creon’s death.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: What is this dress they wear, suited to the dead?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Megara: It is the garb of death we have already put on.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: And were you being forced to die? O woe is me!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Megara: Yes, deserted by every friend, and informed that you were dead.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: What put such desperate thoughts into your heads?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Megara: That was what the heralds of Eurystheus kept proclaiming.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Why did you leave my hearth and home?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Megara: He forced us; your father was dragged from his bed.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Had he no shame, to ill-use the old man so?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Megara: Shame indeed! that goddess and he dwell far enough apart.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Was I so poor in friends in my absence?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Megara: Who are the friends of a man in misfortune?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Do they make so light of my hard warring with the Minyans?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Megara: Misfortune, to repeat it to you, has no friends.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Cast from your heads these chaplets of death, look up to the light, for instead of the darkness below your eyes behold the welcome sun.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: I, meanwhile, since here is work for my hand, will first go raze this upstart tyrant’s halls, and when I have beheaded the villain, I will throw him to dogs to tear; and every Theban who I find has played the traitor after my kindness,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: will I destroy with this victorious club; the rest will I tear apart with my feathered shafts and fill Ismenus full of bloody corpses, and Dirce’s clear stream shall run red with gore. For whom ought I to help rather than wife
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and children and aged father? Farewell my labors! for it was in vain I accomplished them rather than helping these. And yet I ought to die in their defence, since they for their father were doomed; or what shall we find so noble in having fought a hydra and a lion
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: at the commands of Eurystheus, if I make no effort to save my own children from death? No longer then, as before, shall I be called Heracles the victor.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus Leader: It is only right that parents should help their children, their aged fathers, and the partners of their marriage.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: My son, it is like you to show your love for your dear ones and your hate for your enemies; only curb excessive hastiness.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: How, father, am I now showing more than fitting haste?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: The king has a host of allies, needy villains though pretending to be rich,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: who sowed dissension and overthrew the state with a view to plundering their neighbors; for the wealth they had in their houses was all spent, dissipated by their sloth. You were seen entering the city; and, that being so, beware that you do not bring your enemies together and be slain unawares.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Little I care if the whole city saw me; but happening to see a bird perched in an unlucky position, from it I learned that some trouble had befallen my house; so on purpose I made my entry to the land by stealth.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: Well done; now, on your arrival, go salute your household altar,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and let your father’s halls behold your face. For soon the king will be here in person to drag away your wife and children and murder them, and to add me to the bloody list. But if you remain on the spot all will go well, and you will profit by this security; but do not rouse
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: your city before you have these matters well in train, my son.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: I will do so; your advice is good; I will enter my house. After my return at length from the sunless den of Hades and the maiden queen of hell, I will not neglect to greet first of all the gods beneath my roof.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: Did you really go to the house of Hades, my son?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Yes, and brought to the light that three-headed monster.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: Did you conquer him in fight, or receive him from the goddess?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: In fight; for I had been lucky enough to witness the rites of the initiated.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: Is the monster really lodged in the house of Eurystheus?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: The grove of Demeter and the city of Hermione have him now.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: Eurystheus does not know that you have returned to the upper world?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: He does not; I came here first to learn your news.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: How is it you were so long beneath the earth?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: I stayed awhile attempting to bring back Theseus from Hades, father.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: Where is he? gone to his native land?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: He set out for Athens , glad to have escaped from the lower world. Come now, children, attend your father to the house. My entering in is fairer in your eyes, I think, than my going out. Oh, take heart,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and no more let the tears stream from your eyes; you too, my wife, collect your courage, cease from fear; leave go my robe; for I cannot fly away, nor have I any wish to flee from those I love. Ah! they do not loose their hold, but cling to my garments
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: all the more; were you on the razor’s edge of danger? Well, I must lead them, taking them by the hand to draw them after me, my little boats, like a ship when towing; for I too do not reject the care of my children; here all mankind are equal; all love their children, both those of high estate
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and those who are nothing; it is wealth that makes distinctions among them; some have, others want; but all the human race loves its offspring.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: Dear to me is youth always, but old age is hanging over my head, a burden heavier
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: than Aetna ’s crags, casting its pall of gloom upon my eyes. Oh! never may the wealth of Asia ’s kings tempt me
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: to barter for houses stored with gold my happy youth, which is in wealth and poverty alike most fair! But old age is gloomy and deadly;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: I hate it; let it sink beneath the waves! Would it had never found its way to the homes and towns of mortal men, but were still drifting on for ever down the wind.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Had the gods shown discernment and wisdom, as mortals count these things, men would have won youth twice over, a visible mark of worth
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: among whomever found, and after death these would have run a double course once more to the sun-light, while the low born would have had a single portion of life;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and thus would it have been possible to distinguish the good and the bad, just as sailors know the number of the stars amid the clouds. But, as it is, the gods have set no certain boundary
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: between good and bad, but time’s onward roll brings increase only to man’s wealth.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Never will I cease to link in one the Graces and the Muses,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: sweetest union. Never may I live among uneducated boors, but ever may I find a place among the crowned!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Yes, still the aged singer lifts up his voice of bygone memories: still is my song of the triumphs of Heracles, whether Bromius the giver of wine is near, or the strains of the seven-stringed lyre and the Libyan pipe are rising;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: not yet will I cease to sing the Muses’ praise, my patrons in the dance.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: The maids of Delos raise their song of joy, circling round the temple gates in honor of Leto’s fair son,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: the graceful dancer; so I with my old lips will cry aloud songs of joy at your palace-doors, like the swan, aged singer; for there is a good
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: theme for minstrelsy; he is the son of Zeus; yet high above his noble birth tower his deeds of prowess, for his toil secured this life of calm for man,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: having destroyed all fearsome beasts.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Lycus: Amphitryon, it is high time you came forth from the palace; you have been too long arraying yourselves in the robes and trappings of the dead. Come, bid the wife and children of Heracles
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: show themselves outside the house, to die on the conditions you yourselves offered.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: Lord, you persecute me in my misery and heap insult upon me over and above the loss of my son; you should have been more moderate in your zeal, though you are my lord and master.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: But since you impose death’s necessity on me, I must acquiesce; what you wish must be done.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Lycus: Now, where is Megara? where are the children of Alcmena’s son?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: She, I believe, so far as I can guess from outside—
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Lycus: What grounds do you have to base your fancy on?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: Is sitting as a suppliant on the altar’s hallowed steps—
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Lycus: Imploring them quite uselessly to save her life.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: And calling on her dead husband, in vain.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Lycus: He is nowhere near, and he certainly will never come.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: No, unless perhaps a god should raise him from the dead.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Lycus: Go to her and bring her from the palace.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: By doing so I should become an accomplice in her murder.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Lycus: Since you have this scruple, I, who have left fear behind, will myself bring out the mother and her children. Follow me, servants,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: that we may joyfully put an end to this delay of our work.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: Then go your way along the path of fate; for what remains, maybe another will provide. Expect for your evil deeds to find some trouble yourself. Ah! my aged friends, he is marching fairly to his doom; soon will he lie entangled in the snare
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: of the sword, thinking to slay his neighbors, the villain! I will go, to see him fall dead; for the sight of a foe being slain and paying the penalty of his misdeeds affords pleasurable feelings.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: Evil has changed sides; he who was once a mighty king is now turning his life backward into the road to Hades. Hail to you! Justice and heavenly retribution.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: At last have you reached the goal where your death will pay the penalty, for your insults against your betters.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Joy makes my tears burst forth. He has come back—
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: which I never once thought in my heart would happen—the prince of the land.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Come, old friends, let us look within to see if someone has met the fate I hope.

passages.text: a warrior-host with shields of brass, who are handing on their realm to children’s children, a divine light to Thebes .

passages.text: the other, Zeus, who came to wed the bride sprung from Perseus; for that marriage of yours, O Zeus, in days gone by has been proved to me a true story beyond all expectation;

passages.text: and time has shown the brightness of Heracles’ strength; for he emerged from caverns beneath the earth after leaving Pluto’s halls below. To me you are a worthier lord

passages.text: than that base-born king, who now lets it be plainly seen in this struggle between armed warriors, whether justice still finds favor in heaven.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: —Ha! see there, my old comrades! is the same wild panic fallen on us all; what phantom is this I see hovering over the house?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: —Fly, fly, bestir your tardy steps! begone! away!

passages.text: —O savior prince, avert calamity from me!

passages.text: Iris: Courage, old men! she, whom you see, is Madness, daughter of Night, and I am Iris, the handmaid of the gods. We have not come to do your city any hurt,

passages.text: but our warfare is against the house of one man only, against him whom they call the son of Zeus and Alcmena. For until he had finished all his grievous labors, Destiny was preserving him, nor would father Zeus ever suffer me or Hera to harm him.

passages.text: But now that he has accomplished the labors of Eurystheus, Hera wishes to brand him with the guilt of shedding kindred blood by slaying his own children, and I wish it also. Come then, unwed maid, child of black Night, harden your heart relentlessly,

passages.text: send forth frenzy upon this man, confound his mind even to the slaying of his children, drive him, goad him wildly on his mad career, shake out the sails of death, that when he has conveyed over Acheron ’s ferry that fair group of children by his own murderous hand,

passages.text: he may learn to know how fiercely against him the wrath of Hera burns and may also experience mine; otherwise, if he should escape punishment, the gods will become as nothing, while man’s power will grow.

passages.text: Madness: Of noble parents was I born, the daughter of Night, sprung from the blood of Ouranos;

passages.text: and these prerogatives I hold, not to use them in anger against friends, nor do I have any joy in visiting the homes of men; and I wish to counsel Hera, before I see her make a mistake, and you too, if you will hearken to my words. This man, against whose house you are sending me, has made himself a name alike in heaven
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and earth; for, after taming pathless wilds and raging sea, he by his single might raised up again the honors of the gods when sinking before man’s impiety; . . . wherefore I counsel you, do not wish him dire mishaps.

passages.text: Iris: Spare us your advice on Hera’s and my schemes.

passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iris: It was not to practice self-control that the wife of Zeus sent you here.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Madness: I call the sun-god to witness that here I am acting against my will; but if indeed I must at once serve you and Hera

passages.text: and follow you in full cry as hounds follow the huntsman, then I will go; neither ocean with its fiercely groaning waves, nor the earthquake, nor the thunderbolt with blast of agony shall be like the headlong rush I will make into the breast of Heracles; through his roof will I burst my way and swoop upon his house,

passages.text: after first slaying his children; nor shall their murderer know that he is killing the children he begot, till he is released from my madness. passages.text: calling on the goddesses of nether hell. Soon will I rouse you to yet wilder dancing and pipe a note of terror in your ear. Soar away, O Iris, to Olympus on your honored course; while I unseen will steal into the halls of Heracles.

passages.text: Chorus: Alas alas! lament; the son of Zeus, flower of your city, is being cut down. Woe to you, Hellas ! that will cast from you your benefactor, and destroy him as he dances in the shrill frenzy of Madness.

passages.text: address to me?

passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: came rushing on the house; say how the children met their sad mischance.

passages.text: There stood his group of lovely children, with his father and Megara; and already the basket was being passed round the altar, and we were keeping holy silence. But just as Alcmena’s son was bringing the torch in his right hand to dip it in the holy water,

passages.text: he stopped without a word. And as their father lingered, his children looked at him; he was no longer himself; his eyes were rolling; he was quite distraught; his eyeballs were bloodshot, and foam was oozing down his bearded cheek.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: He spoke with a madman’s laugh: Father, why should I offer the purifying flame before I have slain Eurystheus, and have the toil twice over? It is the work of my unaided arm to settle these things well; as soon as I have brought the head of Eurystheus here,

passages.text: I will cleanse my hands for those already slain. Spill the water, cast the baskets from your hands. Ho! give me now my bow and club! To Mycenae will I go; I must take crow-bars and pick-axes, for I will shatter again

passages.text: with iron levers those city-walls which the Cyclopes squared with red plumb-line and mason’s tools.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Then he set out, and though he had no chariot there, he thought he had, and was for mounting to its seat, and using a goad as though his fingers really held one.

passages.text: A twofold feeling filled his servants’ breasts, amusement and fear at once; and one looking to his neighbor said: Is our master making sport for us, or is he mad? But he was pacing to and fro in his house; and, rushing into the men’s chamber, he said he had reached the city of Nisus;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and going into the house, he threw himself upon the floor, as he was, and made ready to feast. But after waiting a brief space he began saying he was on his way to the plains amid the valleys of the Isthmus; and then stripping himself of his mantle,

passages.text: he fell to competing with no one, and he proclaimed himself victor with his own voice, calling on no one to listen. Next, fancy carrying him to Mycenae, he was uttering fearful threats against Eurystheus. Meantime his father caught him by his stalwart arm, and thus addressed him:
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: My son, what do you mean by this? What strange doings are these? Can it be that the blood of your late victims has driven you frantic? But he, supposing it was the father of Eurystheus striving in abject supplication to touch his hand: thrust him aside, and then against his own children aimed his bow
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and made ready his quiver, thinking to slay the sons of Eurystheus. And they in wild fright darted here and there, one to his hapless mother’s skirts, another to the shadow of a pillar, while a third cowered beneath the altar like a bird.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Then cried their mother: O you who begot them, what are you doing? do you mean to slay your children? Likewise his aged father and all the gathered servants cried aloud. But he, hunting the child round and round the column, in dreadful circles, and coming face to face with him shot him to the heart; and he fell upon his back,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: sprinkling the stone pillars with blood as he gasped out his life. Then Heracles shouted in triumph and boasted loud: Here lies one of Eurystheus’ brood dead at my feet, atoning for his father’s hatred. Then he aimed his bow against a second, who had crouched

passages.text: at the altar’s foot thinking to escape unseen. But before he fired, the poor child threw himself at his father’s knees, and, flinging his hand to reach his beard or neck, cried: Oh! hear me, dearest father, do not kill me! I am your child, your own; it is no son of Eurystheus you will slay.

passages.text: But that other, with savage Gorgon-scowl, as the child now stood in range of his baleful archery, smote him on the head, as a smith strikes his molten iron, bringing down his club upon the fair-haired boy, and crushed the bones. The second caught,

passages.text: away he goes to add a third victim to the other two. But before he could, the poor mother caught up her child and carried him within the house and shut the doors. passages.text: with one shaft laid low his wife and child. Then in wild gallop he starts to slay his aged father; but there came a phantom, as it seemed to us on-lookers, of Pallas, with plumed helm, brandishing a spear; and she hurled a rock against the breast of Heracles,

passages.text: which held him from his frenzied thirst for blood and plunged him into sleep; to the ground he fell, striking his back against a column that had fallen on the floor shattered in two when the roof fell in.

passages.text: Then we rallied from our flight, and with the old man’s aid bound him fast with knotted cords to the pillar, so that on his awakening he might do no further mischief. So there he sleeps, poor wretch! a sleep that is not blessed, having murdered wife and children; no, for my part
