passages.text: both kept me safe and were kept safe by me? Surely I have not come a second time to Hades’ halls, having just returned from there for Eurystheus? To Hades? From where? No, I do not see Sisyphus with his stone, or Pluto, or his queen, Demeter’s child.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Surely I am distraught; where am I, so helpless? Ho, there! which of my friends is near or far to cure me in my perplexity? For I have no clear knowledge of things once familiar.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: My aged friends, shall I approach the scene of my sorrow?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus Leader: Yes, and let me go with you, not desert you in your trouble.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Father, why do you weep and veil your eyes, standing far from your beloved son?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: My child! mine still, for all your misery.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Why, what is there so sad in my case that you weep?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: That which might make any of the gods weep, if he were to learn it.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: A bold assertion that, but you are not yet explaining what has happened.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: Your own eyes see that, if by this time you are restored to your senses.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Fill in your sketch if any change awaits my life.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: I will explain, if you are no longer mad as a fiend of hell.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Oh! what suspicions these dark hints of yours again excite!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: I am still doubtful whether you are in your sober senses.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: I have no recollection of being mad.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: Am I to loose my son, old friends, or what shall I do?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Loose me, yes, and say who bound me; for I feel shame at this.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: Rest content with what you know of your woes; the rest forego.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: No. for is silence sufficient to learn what I wish?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: O Zeus, do you behold these deeds proceeding from the throne of Hera?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: What! have I suffered something from her enmity?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: A truce to the goddess! attend to your own troubles.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: I am undone; you will tell me some mischance.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: See here the corpses of your children.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: O horror! what sight is here? ah me!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: My son, against your children you have waged unnatural war.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: War! what do you mean? who killed these?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: You and your bow and some god, whoever is to blame.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: What are you saying? what have I done? Speak, father, you messenger of evil!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: You were insane; it is a sad explanation you are asking.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Was it I that slew my wife also?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: Your own unaided arm has done all this.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Alas! a cloud of mourning wraps me round.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: For this reason I lament your fate.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Did I dash my house to pieces in my frenzy?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: I know nothing but this, that you are utterly undone.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Where did the madness seize me? where did it destroy me?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: When you were purifying yourself with fire at the altar.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Ah me! why do I spare my own life when I have become the murderer of my dear children? Shall I not hasten to leap from some sheer rock, or aim the sword against my heart
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and avenge my children’s blood, or burn my body, which she drove mad, in the fire and so avert from my life the infamy which now awaits me?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: But here I see Theseus coming to check my deadly counsels, my kinsman and friend.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Now shall I stand revealed, and the dearest of my friends will see the pollution I have incurred by my children’s murder. Ah, woe is me! what am I to do? Where can I find freedom from my sorrows? shall I take wings or plunge beneath the earth? Come, let me veil my head in darkness;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: for I am ashamed of the evil I have done, and, since for these I have incurred fresh blood-guiltiness, I do not want to harm the innocent.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: I have come, and others with me, young warriors from the land of Athens , encamped at present by the streams of Asopus,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: to bring an allied army to your son, old friend. For a rumour reached the city of the Erechtheidae, that Lycus had usurped the scepter of this land and had become your enemy even to battle. Wherefore I came making recompense for the former kindness of Heracles
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: in saving me from the world below, if you have any need of such aid as I or my allies can give, old man.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Ha! why this heap of dead upon the floor? Surely I have not delayed too long and come too late to check a revolution? Who slew these children?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: whose wife is this I see? Boys do not go to battle; no, it must be some other strange mischance I here discover.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: O king, whose home is that olive-clad hill!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: Why this piteous prelude in addressing me?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: The gods have afflicted us with grievous suffering.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: Whose are these children, over whom you weep?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: My own son’s children, woe is him! he was their father and butcher both, hardening his heart to the bloody deed.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: Hush! good words only!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: I would I could obey!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: What dreadful words!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: Fortune has spread her wings, and we are ruined, ruined.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: What do you mean? what has he done?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: Slain them in a wild fit of frenzy
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: with arrows dipped in the venom of the hundred-headed hydra.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: This is Hera’s work; but who lies there among the dead, old man?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: My son, my own enduring son, that marched with gods to Phlegra’s plain, there to battle with giants and slay them, warrior that he was.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: Ah, ah! whose fortune was ever so cursed as his?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: Never will you find another mortal that has suffered more or been driven harder.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: Why does he veil his head, poor wretch, in his robe?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: He is ashamed to meet your eye;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: his kinsman’s kind intent and his children’s blood make him abashed.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: But I come to sympathize; uncover him.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: My son, remove that mantle
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: from your eyes, throw it from you, show your face to the sun. As a counterweight, fighting along with my tears, I entreat you as a suppliant, as I grasp your beard, your knees, your hands, and let fall
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: the tear from my old eyes. O my child! restrain your savage lion-like temper, for you are rushing forth on an unholy course of bloodshed, eager to join mischief to mischief, child.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: What! Enough! To you I call who are huddled there in your misery,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: show to your friends your face; for no darkness is black enough to hide your sad mischance. Why do you wave your hand at me, signifying murder? is it that I may not be polluted by speaking with you?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: If I share your misfortune, what is that to me? For once I had good fortune with you. I must refer to the time when you brought me safe from the dead to the light of life. I hate a friend whose gratitude grows old; one who is ready to enjoy his friends’ prosperity
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: but unwilling to sail in the same ship with them when they are unfortunate. Arise, unveil your head, poor wretch! and look on me. The gallant soul endures such blows as heaven deals and does not refuse them.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: O Theseus, did you see this struggle with my children?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: I heard of it, and now I see the horrors you mean.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Why then have you unveiled my head to the sun?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: Why have I? you, a mortal, can not pollute what is of the gods.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Try to escape, luckless wretch, from my unholy taint.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: The avenging fiend does not go forth from friend to friend.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: For this I thank you; I do not regret the service I did you.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: While I, for kindness then received, now show my pity for you.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Ah yes! I am piteous object, a murderer of my sons.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: I weep for you in your changed fortunes.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Did you ever find another more afflicted?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: Your misfortunes reach from earth to heaven.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Therefore I am resolved on death.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: Do you suppose the gods attend to your threats?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: The god has been remorseless to me; so I will be the same to the gods.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: Hush! lest your presumption add to your sufferings.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: My ship is freighted full with sorrow; there is no room to stow anything further.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: What will you do? Where is your fury drifting you?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: I will die and return to that world below from which I have just come.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: Such language is fit for any common fellow.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Ah! yours is the advice of one outside sorrow.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: Are these indeed the words of Heracles, the much-enduring?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Though never so much as this. Endurance must have a limit.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: Is this the benefactor and great friend to mortals?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Mortals bring no help to me; no! Hera has her way.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: Never would Hellas allow you to die through sheer perversity.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Hear me a moment, that I may enter the contest with arguments in answer to your admonitions; and I will unfold to you why life now as well as formerly has been unbearable to me. First I am the son of a man who incurred the guilt of blood, before he married my mother Alcmena,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: by slaying her aged father. Now when the foundation is badly laid at birth, it is necessary for the race to be cursed with woe; and Zeus, whoever this Zeus may be, begot me as an enemy to Hera; yet do not be vexed, old man;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: for you rather than Zeus I regard as my father. Then while I was being suckled, that bedfellow of Zeus foisted into my cradle fearsome snakes to cause my death. After I took on a cloak of youthful flesh,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: of all the toils I then endured what need to tell? what did I not destroy, whether lions, or triple-bodied Typhons, or giants or the battle against the hosts of four-legged Centaurs? or how when I had killed the hydra,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: that monster with a ring of heads with power to grow again, I passed through a herd of countless other toils besides and came to the dead to fetch to the light at the bidding of Eurystheus the three-headed hound, hell’s porter. Last, ah, woe is me! I have dared this labor,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: to crown the sorrows of my house with my children’s murder. I have come to this point of necessity; no longer may I dwell in Thebes , the city that I love; for suppose I stay, to what temple or gathering of friends shall I go? For mine is no curse that invites greetings.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Shall I go to Argos ? how can I, when I am an exile from my country? Well, is there a single other city I can rush to? Am I then to be looked at askance as a marked man, held by cruel stabbing tongues: Is not this the son of Zeus that once murdered children
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and wife? Plague take him from the land!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Now to one who was once called happy, such changes are a grievous thing; though he who is always unfortunate feels no such pain, for sorrow is his birthright. This, I think, is the piteous pass I shall one day come to;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: for earth will cry out forbidding me to touch her, the sea and the river-springs will refuse me a crossing, and I shall become like Ixion who revolves in chains upon that wheel. And so this is best, that I should be seen by no one of the Hellenes,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: among whom in happier days I lived in bliss. What right have I to live? what profit can I have in the possession of a useless, impious life? So let that noble wife of Zeus dance, beating her foot in its shoe;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: for now has she worked her heart’s desire in utterly confounding the first of Hellas ’ sons. Who would pray to such a goddess? Her jealousy of Zeus for his love of a woman has destroyed
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: the benefactors of Hellas , guiltless though they were.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus Leader: This is the work of none other of the gods than the wife of Zeus; you are right in that surmise.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: I cannot counsel you . . . rather than to go on suffering. There is not a man alive that has wholly escaped misfortune’s taint,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: nor any god either, if what poets sing is true. Have they not intermarried in ways that law forbids? Have they not thrown fathers into ignominious chains to gain the sovereign power? Still they inhabit Olympus and brave the issue of their crimes.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: And yet what shall you say in your defence, if you, a child of man, take your fate excessively hard, while they, as gods, do not? No, then, leave Thebes in compliance with the law, and come with me to the city of Pallas. There, when I have purified you of your pollution,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: I will give you homes and the half of all I have. Yes, I will give you all those presents I received from the citizens for saving their fourteen children, when I slew the bull of Crete ; for I have plots of land assigned me throughout the country; these shall henceforth
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: be called after you by men, while you live; and at your death, when you have gone to Hades’ halls, the whole city of Athens shall exalt your honor with sacrifices and a monument of stone. For it is a noble crown of a good reputation
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: for citizens to win from Hellas , by helping a man of worth. This is the return that I will make you for saving me, for now you are in need of friends. But when the gods honor a man, he has no need of friends; for the god’s aid, when he chooses to give it, is enough.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: No! this is quite beside the question of my troubles. For my part, I do not believe that the gods indulge in unholy unions; and as for putting bonds on hands, I have never thought that worthy of credit nor will I now be so persuaded, nor again that one god is naturally lord and master of another.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: For the deity, if he be really such, has no wants; these are miserable tales of the poets. But I, for all my piteous plight, reflected whether I should let myself be branded as a coward for giving up my life. For whoever does not withstand disasters
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: will never be able to withstand even a man’s weapon. I will be steadfast in living; I will go to your city, with grateful thanks for all you offer me.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: But I have tasted of countless troubles, as is well known; never yet did I faint at any or shed a single tear; no, nor did I ever think
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: that I should come to this, to let the tear-drop fall. But now, it seems, I must be fortune’s slave. Well, let it pass; my old father, you see me go forth to exile, and in me you see my own children’s murderer.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Give them burial, and lay them out in death with the tribute of a tear, for the law forbids my doing so. Rest their heads upon their mother’s bosom and fold them in her arms, sad fellowship, which I, alas! unwittingly did slay. And when you have buried these dead,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: live on here still, in bitterness maybe, but still constrain your soul to share my sorrows. O children! he who begot you, your own father, has been your destroyer, and you have had no profit of my triumphs, all my restless toil to win for you by force
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: a fair name, a glorious advantage from a father. You too, unhappy wife, this hand has slain, a poor return to make you for preserving the honor of my bed so safely, for all the weary watch you long have kept within my house. Alas for you, my wife, my sons! alas for me,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: how sad my lot, cut off from wife and child! Ah! these kisses, bitter-sweet! these weapons which it is pain to own! I am not sure whether to keep or let them go; dangling at my side they thus will say,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: With us you destroyed children and wife; we are your children’s slayers, and you keep us. Shall I carry them after that? what answer can I make? Yet, am I to strip myself of these weapons, the comrades of my glorious career in Hellas , and put myself in the power of my foes, to die a death of shame?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: No! I must not let them go, but keep them, though it grieves me. In one thing, Theseus, help my misery; come to Argos and help me to manage the conveyance of the wretched dog; lest, if I go all alone, my sorrow for my sons may do me some hurt.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: O land of Cadmus, and all you people of Thebes !
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: cut off your hair, and mourn with me; go to my children’s burial, and with one dirge lament us all, the dead and me; for on all of us has Hera inflicted the same cruel blow of destruction.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: Rise, unhappy man! you have had your fill of tears.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: I cannot rise; my limbs are rooted here.

passages.text: Theseus: Yes, even the strong are overthrown by misfortunes.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Ah! Would I could become a stone upon this spot, oblivious of trouble.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: Peace! give your hand to a friend and helper.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: No, let me not wipe off the blood upon your robe.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: Wipe it off and spare not; I will not refuse you.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Bereft of my own sons, I find you as a son to me.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: Throw your arm about my neck; I will be your guide.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: A pair of friends indeed, but one a man of sorrows. Ah! aged father, this is the kind of man to make a friend.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: Blessed in her sons, the country that gave him birth!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Theseus, turn me back again to see my children.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: What for? Do you think to find a drug in this to soothe your soul?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: I long to do so, and would embrace my father.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: Here am I, my son; your wish is no less dear to me.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: Have you so short a memory for your troubles?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: All that I endured before was easier to bear than this.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: If anyone sees you play the woman, they will scoff.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Have I by living grown so abject in your sight? It was not so once, I think.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: Yes, too much so; in your sickness you are not the glorious Heracles.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: What about you? What kind of hero were you when in trouble in the world below?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: I was worse than anyone as far as courage went.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: How then can you say of me, that I am abased by my troubles?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Theseus: Forward!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Farewell, my aged father!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: Farewell to you, my son!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: Bury my children as I said.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: But who will bury me, my son?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: I will.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Amphitryon: When wil you come?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles: After you have buried my children.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: I will fetch you from Thebes to Athens . But carry my children within, a grievous burden to the earth. And I, after ruining my house by deeds of shame, will follow as a little boat in the wake of Theseus, a total wreck.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Whoever prefers wealth or might to the possession of good friends, thinks wrongly.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: With grief and many a bitter tear we go our way, robbed of all we prized most dearly.
